# db-08 — DataBall must return columnar and streaming reads

`Filter` returns a fully loaded `List<Dictionary>` (`src/DataBall/DataBall.Filter.cs:45`), and `Open` buffers every row a handler yields before one `AddRows` (`src/DataBall/DataBall.Open.cs:84-91`). Add `ReadColumns(filter)`, which returns typed column arrays with a null mask, and `ReadRowsAsync(filter)`, which streams rows. `Open` writes handler rows in batches.

**Findings:** owner interview (2026-10-08) · **Size:** M · **Tree:** databall

**2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): ReadColumns returns T[] Values plus bool[]? Nulls per column (Nulls null when the column has none).

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-08 relay review): (1) a column created from an all-null handler batch with no config type is widened automatically when a later batch brings its first typed value (ALTER ... TYPE in that batch's transaction; safe because every stored value is NULL). (2) ReadColumns uses a complete read-side type map, separate from import typing: SMALLINT/TINYINT/UTINYINT/USMALLINT -> int, UINTEGER -> long, DECIMAL/UBIGINT/HUGEINT -> double, everything else -> string; it never throws on type, and any remaining error names the column.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:** consolidating `Query`/`Filter`/`Count` with the new reads (db-16); many-file sessions (db-11); Parquet views (db-09); host changes (squalplot sp-03 follows this slice).

## Why

Goals: hosts read typed columns or streamed rows with projection and filter pushdown (suite `docs/databall-v1.4-alignment.md`: "Read API for hosts: both columnar typed arrays (plots) and streaming rows").

Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): nulls are a mask. Each column has `T[] Values` plus `bool[]? Nulls`, which is null when the column has no nulls. There is no boxing and no NaN convention, and plots skip masked points.

Today projection and predicates already push down to DuckDB through `SessionFilter` (`DataBall.Filter.cs:89-102`); only the materialization is the problem.

## Files

- `src/DataBall/ColumnSet.cs` (new): `ColumnSet` (`long RowCount`, `IReadOnlyList<ColumnData> Columns`, indexer by name, case-insensitive) and `ColumnData` (`string Name`, `Type ElementType`, `bool[]? Nulls`, `Array Values`) with `ColumnData<T> : ColumnData` exposing `T[] Values`. Element types come from `DuckDbStore.FromDuckDbType` (`src/DataBall/DuckDbStore.cs:1446`). A null slot holds `default(T)` and `Nulls[i] = true`.
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.Filter.cs`: `public ColumnSet ReadColumns(SessionFilter filter)` and `public IAsyncEnumerable<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>> ReadRowsAsync(SessionFilter filter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`, both built on `BuildSelectSql` (`:89`).
- `src/DataBall/DuckDbStore.cs`: a reader-based read path. `ReadColumns` sizes its arrays from one `COUNT(*)` with the same predicates, then fills them from a `DbDataReader`. `ReadRowsAsync` uses DuckDB.NET streaming mode (`DuckDBCommand.UseStreamingMode`; confirm it exists in 1.5.5, and if not, record the deviation and fall back to the reader without it). The session counts open streams; any write while a stream is open throws `DataBallException`.
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.Open.cs`: drain `handler.Parse` in batches of `HandlerBatchSize` (internal, 10,000) through `AddRows`; an internal test hook `AfterHandlerBatchForTests`.
- `README.md` ("Library usage", "Query") and `docs/how-it-works.md`.
- Tests: new `tests/DataBall.Tests/ReadTests.cs`; batching in `HandlerTests`.
- No new dependencies.

## Failing tests

In `ReadTests` unless noted; each asserts:

1. `ReadColumns_TypedArrays_MatchQuery`: `long`, `double`, `bool`, `DateTime` and `string` columns equal `Query` output element by element, and each `ColumnData` has the expected `ElementType`.
2. `ReadColumns_NullMask`: a column with nulls has `Nulls` set exactly at those rows; a column without nulls has `Nulls == null`.
3. `ReadColumns_ProjectionAndPredicates`: only the requested columns, in request order; only matching rows.
4. `ReadColumns_LayoutSession_ReadsThroughView`.
5. `ReadColumns_UnknownColumn_Throws` (`DataBallException`).
6. `ReadRowsAsync_RowsEqualFilter`: same rows and order (with `ORDER BY` through a predicate-free filter over a sorted fixture) as `Filter`.
7. `ReadRowsAsync_EarlyBreak_ReleasesReader`: break after one row of a 1M-row `range()` session, then a write succeeds.
8. `ReadRowsAsync_WriteDuringEnumeration_Throws`.
9. `ReadRowsAsync_Cancellation_ThrowsOperationCanceled`.
10. `Open_Handler_WritesInBatches` (`HandlerTests`): a test handler yields 25,000 rows; the hook sees batches of 10,000, 10,000 and 5,000; the row count is 25,000.
11. `Open_Handler_FailureAfterFirstBatch_Throws_NoLeak` (`HandlerTests`): `Open` throws `DataBallException`, and a file-backed path used by the session can be opened again.

1. `slicer start db-08 --render --strict`. Write tests 1–11; run them and record each red line.

3. `ReadColumns`, then `ReadRowsAsync` with the open-stream guard on every write path (`ThrowIfReadOnly` call sites).
4. Batched handler drain in `OpenAsync`.
